title: Charing railway station
extract: Charing railway station serves the village of  Charing in Kent, England. It is 53 miles 11 chains (85.5 km) down the line from London Victoria.
categories: Category:Former London, Chatham and Dover Railway stations
Category:Railway stations in Great Britain opened in 1884
Category:Transport in the Borough of Ashford

title: Charing
extract: Charing () is a village and civil parish in the Ashford district of Kent, in south-east England. It includes the settlements of Charing Heath and Westwell Leacon.
categories: Category:Villages in the Borough of Ashford

title: Archbishop's Palace, Charing
extract: Archbishop's Palace, Charing, is a scheduled monument in Charing, Kent, England. The palace is an important heritage site dating back to the eighth century, and one of the earliest to be owned by the see of Canterbury.
categories: Category:Episcopal palaces of archbishops of Canterbury
Category:Religious buildings and structures completed in the 1340s

title: Charing Beech Hangers
extract:
Charing Beech Hangers is a 52.6-hectare (130-acre) biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north of Ashford in Kent.
This steeply sloping site has mature beech and oak, and the ground flora is varied with some uncommon species.
categories: Category:Sites of Special Scientific Interest in Kent

title: Eastwell, Kent
extract: Eastwell is a hamlet and civil parish about 3 miles (5 km) north of Ashford, Kent, England. The 2011 Census recorded the parish's population as 103.

title: St Mary's Church, Eastwell
extract: St Mary's Church is a ruined former Church of England parish church, in the grounds of Eastwell Park in the hamlet of Eastwell, Kent, England. It is recorded in the National Heritage List for England as a designated Grade II listed building, and is a Scheduled monument.
categories: Category:19th-century Church of England church buildings
Category:Churches preserved by the Friends of Friendless Churches
Category:Grade II listed churches in Kent

title: Eastwell Park
extract: Eastwell Park is a large area of parkland and a country estate in the civil parish of Eastwell, adjoining Ashford, Kent, in England. It was owned by the Earls of Winchilsea for more than three centuries.
categories: Category:Grade II listed buildings in Kent
Category:Royal residences in the United Kingdom

title: Saint Christopher's Church, Boughton Lees
extract:
Saint Christopher's Church is a mediaeval Grade II listed church in Boughton Lees near Ashford, Kent, part of the Church of England.
The building was originally a mediaeval hall house.
categories: Category:Church of England church buildings in Kent

title: Boughton Lees
extract: Boughton Lees is a village in the civil parish of Boughton Aluph, Ashford District, Kent, England. It stands on the main Ashford-Faversham road, some 3.5 miles (5.6 km) north of Ashford.
categories: Category:Villages in the Borough of Ashford

title: Stour Music Festival
extract: The Stour Music Festival is a festival of early music held in the Stour valley, Kent, England, founded by countertenor Alfred Deller in 1962. The principal venue is a medieval church, All Saints' Church, Boughton Aluph.

title: All Saints' Church, Boughton Aluph
extract: All Saints' Church is a 13th-century pilgrims' Grade I listed church in Boughton Aluph near Ashford, Kent. It is part of the Church of England.
categories: Category:Church of England church buildings in Kent
Category:Grade I listed buildings in Kent

title: Boughton Aluph
extract: Boughton Aluph (pronounced Bawton Alluf) is a village and civil parish in the Borough of Ashford in Kent, England, and is about 5 miles (8 km) north of Ashford on the A251 road. There are two villages within the parish: Boughton Aluph itself, and Boughton Lees.

title: Molash
extract: Molash is a civil parish and village in Kent, South East England. It contains a small part of an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty (AONB) - the North Downs - and is on the A252 road between Canterbury, Ashford and Faversham.
categories: Category:Villages in the Borough of Ashford

title: Chilham Castle
extract: Chilham Castle is a Jacobean manor house and keep in the village of Chilham, between Ashford and Canterbury in the county of Kent, England. The keep is of Norman origin and dates to 1174, although it may have been built on an older Anglo-Saxon fortification.
categories: Category:Grade I listed houses in Kent

title: Chilham
extract: Chilham is a village and civil parish in the Borough of Ashford in Kent, England. It sits on the north bank of the Great Stour around 5+1⁄2 miles (9 kilometres) to the southwest of Canterbury and seven miles (eleven kilometres) northeast of Ashford.

title: Chilham railway station
extract: Chilham railway station is a railway station in Chilham, Kent. It is on the Ashford to Ramsgate line between Ashford International and Canterbury West.
categories: Category:Railway stations in Great Britain opened in 1846
Category:Transport in the Borough of Ashford

title: Julliberrie's Grave
extract: Julliberrie's Grave, also known as The Giant's Grave or The Grave, is an unchambered long barrow located near to the village of Chilham in the south-eastern English county of Kent. Probably constructed in the fourth millennium BCE, during Britain's Early Neolithic period, today it survives only in a state of ruin.

title: Broadham Down
extract: Broadham Down is a  16-hectare (40-acre) nature reserve east of Chilham and west of Canterbury in Kent. It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

title: Chartham railway station
extract: Chartham railway station is in Chartham, Kent, on the Ashford to Ramsgate line. The station, and all trains serving it, is operated by Southeastern.
categories: Category:Railway stations in Great Britain opened in 1850

title: Church of St Mary, Chartham
extract: St Mary's Church is in the village of Chartham, Kent, England.  It is an active Anglican parish church in the Diocese of Canterbury.
categories: Category:Church of England church buildings in Kent
Category:Grade I listed churches in Kent

title: Chartham
extract: Chartham is a village and civil parish in the Canterbury district of Kent, England. It is situated on the Ashford side of the city, and is in the North Downs area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, 2.3 mi (4 km) south west of Canterbury, England.

title: Thanington
extract: Thanington is a civil parish on the west edge of Canterbury, Kent, United Kingdom. It extends to the south-west of A2 from Wincheap to the Milton Bridge in Chartham.

title: Canterbury Parkway railway station
extract: Canterbury Parkway railway station is a proposed interchange between the Ashford–Ramsgate line and the Chatham Main Line near Canterbury, Kent.

title: Whitehall Meadows
extract: Whitehall Meadows is a  11.6-hectare (29-acre) Local Nature Reserve in Canterbury in Kent. It is owned and managed by Canterbury City Council.

title: Canterbury Academy
extract: The Canterbury Academy is a co-educational 11-19 academy school in Canterbury, Kent, England. It is a specialist Sports College and 15% of its 1081 pupils are selected on musical aptitude.
categories: Category:Educational institutions in the United Kingdom established in 2010

title: Whitehall Dyke
extract:
Whitehall Dyke is a tributary of the Great Stour river in Kent, England.
The stream runs from its source near Harbledown, 5.6 kilometres, to the Great Stour at Thanington Without near Canterbury.

title: Canterbury Castle
extract: Canterbury Castle is a ruined Norman castle in Canterbury, Kent, England (grid reference TR14545743). It is a five-minute walk from Canterbury East Station and the main bus station around City Wall.
categories: Category:Grade I listed buildings in Kent

title: St Mildred's Church, Canterbury
extract: The Church of Saint Mildred is a partly Anglo-Saxon stone church in Canterbury probably dating from the 11th century. It has been a Grade I listed building since 1949.
categories: Category:Churches with elements of Anglo-Saxon work
Category:Grade I listed churches in Kent

title: St. Dunstan's, Canterbury
extract: St. Dunstan's is an Anglican church in Canterbury, Kent, at the junction of London Road and Whitstable Road.
categories: Category:Church of England church buildings in Kent
Category:Grade I listed churches in Kent

title: Greyfriars, Canterbury
extract: Greyfriars in Canterbury was the first Franciscan friary in England.

title: Canterbury Heritage Museum
extract: The Canterbury Heritage Museum (formerly the Museum of Canterbury) was a museum in Stour Street, Canterbury, South East England, telling the history of the city. It was housed in the 12th-century Poor Priests' Hospital next to the River Stour.
categories: Category:Children's museums in the United Kingdom
Category:Grade II listed buildings in Kent
Category:Mass media museums in the United Kingdom

title: Kent Museum of Freemasonry
extract:
The Kent Museum of Freemasonry, is a museum in St Peters Place, Canterbury, Kent with  a rare collection of masonic exhibits of national and international importance.
It tells the history of Freemasonry from its inception through to the modern day, with emphasis on Kent, its Lodges and their origins and has possibly the finest collection of Masonic material in the UK outside London.

title: Canterbury Guildhall
extract: Canterbury Guildhall, formerly the Church of the Holy Cross, is a municipal building in St Peter's Place in Canterbury, Kent, England. The structure, which is the meeting place of Canterbury City Council, is a Grade II* listed building.
categories: Category:City and town halls in Kent
Category:Government buildings completed in the 14th century
Category:Grade II* listed buildings in Kent

title: Canterbury city walls
extract: Canterbury city walls are a sequence of defensive walls built around the city of Canterbury in Kent, England. The first city walls were built by the Romans, probably between 270 and 280 AD. These walls were constructed from stone on top of an earth bank, and protected by a ditch and wall towers.
categories: Category:City walls in the United Kingdom

title: Westgate, Canterbury
extract: The Westgate is a medieval gatehouse in Canterbury, Kent, England. This 60-foot (18 m) high western gate of the city wall is the largest surviving city gate in England.
categories: Category:City walls in the United Kingdom
Category:Grade I listed buildings in Kent
Category:Military and war museums in England
Category:Prison museums in the United Kingdom

title: Fleur de Lis Hotel
extract: Fleur de Lis Hotel was a 13th century hotel in the city of Canterbury, Kent, England. It is recorded that Charles Dickens stayed there.
categories: Category:Demolished hotels in the United Kingdom

title: Beaney House of Art and Knowledge
extract: The Beaney House of Art and Knowledge is the central museum, library and art gallery of the city of Canterbury, Kent, England. It is housed in a Grade II listed building.
categories: Category:Art museums and galleries in Kent
Category:Grade II listed buildings in Kent

title: Canterbury West railway station
extract: Canterbury West railway station is a Grade II listed railway station, and the busier of the two stations in Canterbury in Kent, England. The station, as well as all services, are operated by Southeastern with both main line and high speed trains serving the station.
categories: Category:Grade II listed buildings in Kent
Category:Railway stations in Great Britain opened in 1846

title: Marlowe Memorial
extract: The Marlowe Memorial is a statue and four statuettes erected in memory of the playwright and poet Christopher Marlowe in 1891 in Canterbury, England. The memorial was commissioned by a Marlowe Memorial Committee, and comprises a bronze statue, The Muse of Poetry sculpted by Edward Onslow Ford, standing on a plinth decorated with statuettes of actors playing Marlowe roles.
categories: Category:1891 establishments in the United Kingdom

title: All Saints Cottage, Canterbury
extract: All Saints Cottage, on All Saints Lane, in Canterbury, Kent, England is a building dating from the 16th century. Its origins and original purpose and configuration are all uncertain; it may have been designed as a single house, or as a range of smaller cottages, or have served some commercial or religious function.
categories: Category:Buildings and structures completed in the 16th century
Category:Grade II listed buildings in Kent

title: Westgate Hall, Canterbury
extract: Westgate Hall is a hundred-year-old drill hall and community space in a Conservation area of Canterbury, Kent, notable for hosting community events. The Hall was threatened with closure or demolition in 2009, but a group of local people fought to save it.

title: Marlowe Theatre
extract: The Marlowe Theatre is a 1,200-seat theatre in Canterbury named after playwright Christopher Marlowe, who was born and attended school in the city. It was named a Stage Awards, 2022 UK Theatre of the Year.

title: Blackfriars, Canterbury
extract: Blackfriars, Canterbury was a priory of the Dominican Order in Kent, England. Founded in 1237 it lay either side of the River Stour in the west of the city, adjacent to where the Marlowe Theatre now stands.
categories: Category:Grade I listed buildings in Kent

title: East Kent
extract: East Kent is a planned unitary authority area in Kent, England. It is planned to be formed on 1 April 2028.

title: Siege of Canterbury
extract: The siege of Canterbury was a major Viking raid on the city of Canterbury that occurred between 8 and 29 September 1011, fought between a Viking army led by Thorkell the Tall and the Anglo-Saxon defenders. The details of the siege are largely unknown, and most of the known events were recorded in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.

title: Canterbury
extract: Canterbury (  KAN-tər-bər-ee or  -⁠berr-ee) is a city and UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Canterbury district, county of Kent, England; it was a county borough until 1974. Lying on the River Stour not far from its mouth on the Strait of Dover, the city has a mild oceanic climate.

title: City of Canterbury
extract: Canterbury (  KAN-tər-bər-ee or  -⁠berr-ee), also known as the City of Canterbury, is a local government district with city status in Kent, England. It is named after its largest settlement, Canterbury, where the council is based.

title: Old Palace, Canterbury
extract: The Old Palace, also referred to as the Archbishop's Palace, is a historic building situated within the precincts of Canterbury Cathedral. It is the main residence of the Archbishop of Canterbury when in Canterbury.
categories: Category:Episcopal palaces of archbishops of Canterbury
Category:Grade I listed houses in Kent

title: Old Synagogue, Canterbury
extract: The Old Synagogue is a former Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 944 King Street in Canterbury, Kent, England, in the United Kingdom. Established in 1720, the congregation worshiped in the Ashkenazi rite until it was dissolved in c. 1911.
categories: Category:19th-century synagogues in the United Kingdom
Category:Egyptian Revival architecture in the United Kingdom
Category:Grade II listed buildings in Kent
Category:Grade II listed religious buildings and structures
Category:Religious buildings and structures in Kent

title: Reginald Pole
extract: Reginald Pole (12 March 1500 – 17 November 1558) was an English cardinal and the last Catholic Archbishop of Canterbury, holding the office from 1556 to 1558 during the Marian Restoration of Catholicism.
categories: Category:Chancellors of the University of Cambridge
Category:Fellows of Corpus Christi College, Oxford
Category:Participants in the Council of Trent

title: Chair of St Augustine
extract: The Chair of St Augustine or Cathedra Augustini (Latin) is the ceremonial enthronement cathedra of the archbishop of Canterbury in Canterbury Cathedral, Kent.
categories: Category:Marble sculptures in the United Kingdom

title: Canterbury Cathedral
extract: Canterbury Cathedral is the cathedral of the archbishop of Canterbury, the spiritual leader of the Church of England and symbolic leader of the worldwide Anglican Communion. Located in Canterbury, Kent, it is on the site of one of the oldest Christian structures in England and forms part of a World Heritage Site.
categories: Category:Church of England church buildings in Kent
Category:Grade I listed buildings in Kent

title: Diocese of Canterbury
extract: The Diocese of Canterbury also referred to as the See of Canterbury is a Church of England diocese covering eastern Kent which was founded by St Augustine of Canterbury in 597. The diocese is centred on Canterbury Cathedral and is the oldest see of the Church of England.
categories: Category:Dioceses of the Church of England

title: The King's School, Canterbury
extract: The King's School is a public school in Canterbury, Kent, England for pupils aged 13-18. It is a member of the Headmasters' and Headmistresses' Conference and the Eton Group.
categories: Category:Buildings and structures completed in the 6th century
Category:Educational institutions established in the 6th century
Category:Member schools of the Headmasters' and Headmistresses' Conference

title: Tomb of Edward, the Black Prince
extract: The tomb of Edward, the Black Prince, was built in the 14th century for Edward of Woodstock (d. 1376).
categories: Category:Buildings and structures completed in the 14th century

title: Trinity Chapel
extract: Trinity Chapel at the east end of Canterbury Cathedral forms part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It was built under the supervision of the master-masons William of Sens and William the Englishman as a shrine for the relics of the martyred Archbishop of Canterbury Thomas Becket.
categories: Category:Church of England church buildings in Kent

title: Bus Company Island
extract: Bus Company Island is a  1.1-hectare (2.7-acre) Local Nature Reserve in Canterbury in Kent. It is owned and managed by Canterbury City Council.

title: Canterbury power station
extract: Canterbury power station supplied electricity to the city of Canterbury, Kent, England, from 1900 to 1960. This small generating station was owned and operated by Canterbury Corporation until the nationalisation of the British electricity supply industry in 1948.
categories: Category:Demolished power stations in the United Kingdom

title: Kingsmead Stadium
extract: Kingsmead Stadium was a greyhound racing and motorcycle speedway track and Association football ground in Canterbury. It was host to Canterbury City F.C. and the Canterbury Crusaders speedway team.
categories: Category:Defunct greyhound racing venues in the United Kingdom
